Locking, concurrency and calling context for all listed ioctls and structures.
State machines and sequencing for freeze and thaw, trim and discard and zero, trace setup start stop teardown, shutdown, clone and dedupe.

findings.text: FS_XFLAG_REALTIME uses value 0x1 and requests realtime volume placement. FS_XFLAG_PREALLOC uses value 0x2 and marks preallocated extents. FS_XFLAG_IMMUTABLE uses value 0x8 and forbids modification. FS_XFLAG_APPEND uses value 0x10 and forces append-only writes. FS_XFLAG_SYNC uses value 0x20 and forces synchronous writes. FS_XFLAG_NOATIME uses value 0x40 and suppresses access-time updates. FS_XFLAG_NODUMP uses value 0x80 and excludes from backups. FS_XFLAG_RTINHERIT uses value 0x100 and inherits realtime on create. FS_XFLAG_PROJINHERIT uses value 0x200 and inherits project id on create. FS_XFLAG_NOSYMLINKS uses value 0x400 and forbids symlink creation.

FS_XFLAG_EXTSIZE uses value 0x800 as extent-size allocator hint. FS_XFLAG_EXTSZINHERIT uses value 0x1000 to inherit extent size. FS_XFLAG_NODEFRAG uses value 0x2000 to suppress defragmentation. FS_XFLAG_FILESTREAM uses value 0x4000 to select filestream allocator. FS_XFLAG_DAX uses value 0x8000 to select direct access I/O. FS_XFLAG_COWEXTSIZE uses value 0x10000 as copy-on-write extent hint. FS_XFLAG_VERITY uses value 0x20000 to mark verity protection. FS_XFLAG_CASEFOLD uses value 0x40000 to allow case-insensitive lookup. FS_XFLAG_CASENONPRESERVING uses value 0x80000 to note case not preserved. FS_XFLAG_HASATTR uses value 0x80000000 as attribute-present marker without DIFLAG counterpart.

Basic block controls share type 0x12 with no transfer payload. BLKROSET number 93 changes read-only state where zero means writable. BLKROGET number 94 reports that state. BLKRRPART number 95 asks reread of partition tables. BLKGETSIZE number 96 reports size in 512-byte units through long. BLKFLSBUF number 97 flushes buffer cache. BLKRASET number 98 and BLKRAGET number 99 set and query device readahead. BLKFRASET number 100 and BLKFRAGET number 101 set and query filesystem readahead. BLKSECTSET number 102 and BLKSECTGET number 103 adjust and report the per-request sector ceiling. BLKSSZGET number 104 reports sector size.

Extended block controls also use type 0x12. BLKBSZGET number 112 reads block size and BLKBSZSET number 113 writes it using word-sized payload. BLKGETSIZE64 number 114 reports byte size through 64-bit payload. BLKTRACESETUP number 115 with trace setup payload plus BLKTRACESTART number 116, BLKTRACESTOP number 117 and BLKTRACETEARDOWN number 118 manage tracing, with BLKTRACESETUP2 number 142 using second-generation setup payload. BLKDISCARD number 119, BLKSECDISCARD number 125 and BLKZEROOUT number 127 discard or zero ranges. BLKIOMIN number 120, BLKIOOPT number 121, BLKALIGNOFF number 122 and BLKPBSZGET number 123 expose topology. BLKDISCARDZEROES number 124 reports discard zeroing, BLKROTATIONAL number 126 reports rotation, and BLKGETDISKSEQ number 128 reports disk sequence through 64-bit payload.

File range and mapping operations use small numeric and lettered encodings. BMAP_IOCTL value 1 remains only for compatibility. FIBMAP type 0 number 1 exposes block mapping and FIGETBSZ type 0 number 2 reports its block size. FIFREEZE type X number 119 with integer payload freezes, FITHAW type X number 120 thaws, and FITRIM type X number 121 trims using range payload. FICLONE type 0x94 number 9 clones by descriptor, FICLONERANGE type 0x94 number 13 clones a range, and FIDEDUPERANGE type 0x94 number 54 deduplicates with bidirectional range payload. FS_IOC_SHUTDOWN type X number 125 with 32-bit payload shuts down filesystem.

Filesystem attribute and identity controls center on flags, version, extended attributes and labels. FS_IOC_GETFLAGS magic f number 1 and FS_IOC_SETFLAGS magic f number 2 exchange long flag words, with 32-bit compat forms FS_IOC32_GETFLAGS and FS_IOC32_SETFLAGS using integer payload. FS_IOC_GETVERSION magic v number 1 and FS_IOC_SETVERSION magic v number 2 exchange long version, with integer compat forms FS_IOC32_GETVERSION and FS_IOC32_SETVERSION. FS_IOC_FIEMAP magic f number 11 exchanges extent maps bidirectionally. FS_IOC_FSGETXATTR magic X number 31 and FS_IOC_FSSETXATTR magic X number 32 exchange extended-attribute structures. Label capacity FSLABEL_MAX is 256 characters, with FS_IOC_GETFSLABEL and FS_IOC_SETFSLABEL type 0x94 numbers 49 and 50 exchanging label buffers, FS_IOC_GETFSUUID type 0x15 number 0 reporting UUID, FS_IOC_GETFSSYSFSPATH type 0x15 number 1 reporting sysfs path, and FS_IOC_GETLBMD_CAP type 0x15 number 2 negotiating block-metadata capability.

FS_SECRM_FL uses value 0x1 for secure deletion. FS_UNRM_FL uses value 0x2 for undelete. FS_COMPR_FL uses value 0x4 for compression. FS_SYNC_FL uses value 0x8 for synchronous updates. FS_IMMUTABLE_FL uses value 0x10 for immutability. FS_APPEND_FL uses value 0x20 for append-only. FS_NODUMP_FL uses value 0x40 to skip dumps. FS_NOATIME_FL uses value 0x80 to suppress access-time. FS_DIRTY_FL uses value 0x100 to mark dirty. FS_COMPRBLK_FL uses value 0x200 to note compressed clusters. FS_NOCOMP_FL uses value 0x400 to suppress compression.

FS_ENCRYPT_FL uses value 0x800 for encryption. FS_BTREE_FL and FS_INDEX_FL share value 0x1000 for indexed directory formats. FS_IMAGIC_FL uses value 0x2000 for special directory magic. FS_JOURNAL_DATA_FL uses value 0x4000 as journal-data reservation. FS_NOTAIL_FL uses value 0x8000 to forbid tail merging. FS_DIRSYNC_FL uses value 0x10000 for directory synchronous behavior. FS_TOPDIR_FL uses value 0x20000 for hierarchy tops. FS_HUGE_FILE_FL uses value 0x40000 as huge-file reservation. FS_EXTENT_FL uses value 0x80000 for extents. FS_VERITY_FL uses value 0x100000 for verity protection. FS_EA_INODE_FL uses value 0x200000 for large extended-attribute inodes. FS_EOFBLOCKS_FL uses value 0x400000 as reservation. FS_NOCOW_FL uses value 0x800000 to disable copy-on-write.

FS_DAX_FL uses value 0x2000000 for direct-access inodes. FS_INLINE_DATA_FL uses value 0x10000000 as inline-data reservation. FS_PROJINHERIT_FL uses value 0x20000000 to inherit project id. FS_CASEFOLD_FL uses value 0x40000000 for case folding. FS_RESERVED_FL uses value 0x80000000 as library reservation. FS_FL_USER_VISIBLE mask 0x3DFFF defines bits exposed to users. FS_FL_USER_MODIFIABLE mask 0x380FF defines bits users may change. SYNC_FILE_RANGE_WAIT_BEFORE is 1, SYNC_FILE_RANGE_WRITE is 2, SYNC_FILE_RANGE_WAIT_AFTER is 4, and SYNC_FILE_RANGE_WRITE_AND_WAIT combines all three phases.

Per-operation read-write flags use bitwise integer type __kernel_rwf_t. RWF_HIPRI is 0x1 for high priority. RWF_DSYNC is 0x2 and RWF_SYNC is 0x4 for durability strengths. RWF_NOWAIT is 0x8 to forbid blocking. RWF_APPEND is 0x10 to force append position and RWF_NOAPPEND is 0x20 to forbid it. RWF_ATOMIC is 0x40 for atomicity. RWF_DONTCACHE is 0x80 to avoid caching. RWF_NOSIGNAL is 0x100 to suppress signals. RWF_SUPPORTED is the union of all nine bits. PROCFS_IOCTL_MAGIC is letter f and types procfs ioctls.

FS_IOC_SHUTDOWN carries filesystem shutdown with 32-bit flags payload. FS_SHUTDOWN_FLAGS_DEFAULT value 0 selects default handling. FS_SHUTDOWN_FLAGS_LOGFLUSH value 0x1 flushes log without data. FS_SHUTDOWN_FLAGS_NOLOGFLUSH value 0x2 flushes neither log nor data.

page_region holds three 64-bit unsigned values in order for scan interval start, scan interval end, and category set. pm_scan_arg holds twelve 64-bit unsigned values in order for structure size, option flags, scan start, scan end, walk completion point, vector address, vector length, page limit, inverted-category set, required-category mask, any-of category mask, and returned-category mask.

Page-scan categories occupy single-bit positions 0 through 9. PAGE_IS_WPALLOWED is bit 0, PAGE_IS_WRITTEN bit 1, PAGE_IS_FILE bit 2, PAGE_IS_PRESENT bit 3, PAGE_IS_SWAPPED bit 4, PAGE_IS_PFNZERO bit 5, PAGE_IS_HUGE bit 6, PAGE_IS_SOFT_DIRTY bit 7, PAGE_IS_GUARD bit 8, PAGE_IS_ACCESSED bit 9. PM_SCAN_WP_MATCHING is bit 0 to write-protect matches and PM_SCAN_CHECK_WPASYNC is bit 1 to abort on non-protectable pages. PAGEMAP_SCAN is a bidirectional procfs ioctl number 16 with scan-argument payload and PROCMAP_QUERY is number 17 with query-structure payload.

procmap_query begins with 64-bit size for compatibility, then 64-bit query flags and 64-bit query address as inputs. Outputs follow as 64-bit virtual start, end, permission flags, page granularity and file offset, plus 64-bit inode number and 32-bit device major and minor. Two 32-bit in-out lengths report name and build-identifier sizes, followed by two 64-bit input addresses for caller buffers receiving name and build identifier. Query flag values single out readable 0x1, writable 0x2, executable 0x4, shared 0x8, covering-or-next 0x10, and file-backed 0x20.

By default procmap lookup returns the area covering the supplied address and permission filtering requires every requested permission bit to be present, so read-only queries match both read-only and writable areas. Covering-or-next modifier falls back to the nearest later area and file-backed modifier restricts to mapped files, combinable for iteration. Caller sets size and input fields while kernel preserves query inputs and fills outputs, zeroes name or identifier lengths when absent, and rejects overlong names or identifiers that exceed supplied buffers. Scan structures use explicit size fields for forward and backward compatibility.

FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_4 is 0, FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_8 is 1, FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_16 is 2, FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_32 is 3 and FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAGS_PAD_MASK is 0x3. FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAG_DIRECT_KEY is 0x4, FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAG_IV_INO_LBLK_64 is 0x8 and FSCRYPT_POLICY_FLAG_IV_INO_LBLK_32 is 0x10. FSCRYPT_MODE_AES_256_XTS is 1, FSCRYPT_MODE_AES_256_CTS is 4, FSCRYPT_MODE_AES_128_CBC is 5, FSCRYPT_MODE_AES_128_CTS is 6, FSCRYPT_MODE_SM4_XTS is 7, FSCRYPT_MODE_SM4_CTS is 8, FSCRYPT_MODE_ADIANTUM is 9 and FSCRYPT_MODE_AES_256_HCTR2 is 10. FSCRYPT_POLICY_V1 is 0, FSCRYPT_POLICY_V2 is 2, FSCRYPT_KEY_DESCRIPTOR_SIZE is 8, FSCRYPT_KEY_IDENTIFIER_SIZE is 16, FSCRYPT_MAX_KEY_SIZE is 64, FSCRYPT_KEY_DESC_PREFIX is fscrypt with trailing colon and FSCRYPT_KEY_DESC_PREFIX_SIZE is 8, FSCRYPT_KEY_SPEC_TYPE_DESCRIPTOR is 1 and FSCRYPT_KEY_SPEC_TYPE_IDENTIFIER is 2.

fscrypt_policy_v1 holds version plus content mode, filename mode, flags and 8-byte descriptor. fscrypt_key holds 32-bit mode, 64-byte raw buffer and 32-bit size. fscrypt_policy_v2 holds version, two modes, flags, log2 data-unit size, three reserved bytes and 16-byte identifier. fscrypt_get_policy_ex_arg holds 64-bit size plus a union offering version byte or full v1 or v2 policy as output. fscrypt_key_specifier holds 32-bit type with reserved word plus a 32-byte union offering descriptor or identifier. Provisioning payload holds type and flags then trailing raw bytes. Add-key argument holds specifier, raw size, key id, flags and seven reserved words then raw bytes. Remove-key argument holds specifier, output removal flags and five reserved words. Get-status argument holds specifier with six reserved inputs plus status code, status flags, user count and thirteen reserved outputs.

FS_IOC_SET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY magic f number 19 takes v1 policy, FS_IOC_GET_ENCRYPTION_PWSALT number 20 returns 16-byte salt, FS_IOC_GET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY number 21 returns v1 policy, FS_IOC_GET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY_EX number 22 negotiates size plus version, FS_IOC_ADD_ENCRYPTION_KEY number 23 adds, FS_IOC_REMOVE_ENCRYPTION_KEY number 24 and FS_IOC_REMOVE_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ALL_USERS number 25 remove, FS_IOC_GET_ENCRYPTION_KEY_STATUS number 26 reports presence, and FS_IOC_GET_ENCRYPTION_NONCE number 27 returns nonce. FSCRYPT_KEY_STATUS_ABSENT is 1, FSCRYPT_KEY_STATUS_PRESENT is 2, FSCRYPT_KEY_STATUS_INCOMPLETELY_REMOVED is 3 with FSCRYPT_KEY_STATUS_FLAG_ADDED_BY_SELF 0x1. FSCRYPT_KEY_REMOVAL_STATUS_FLAG_FILES_BUSY is 0x1, FSCRYPT_KEY_REMOVAL_STATUS_FLAG_OTHER_USERS is 0x2 and FSCRYPT_ADD_KEY_FLAG_HW_WRAPPED is 0x1.

FS_BTREE_FL and FS_INDEX_FL denote the same numeric value, so either name selects indexed directories. RWF_SUPPORTED equals the union of the nine read-write bits and SYNC_FILE_RANGE_WRITE_AND_WAIT equals the union of its three phase bits. FSLABEL_MAX bounds label buffers while each filesystem may impose a smaller limit. Encryption policy version byte discriminates v1 versus v2 layout and key specifier type discriminates descriptor versus identifier, with policy query size acting as bidirectional length handshake and add-key flags plus reserved words preserving extension space.

Label and name handling risks truncation because interface maximum differs from per-filesystem limits and overlong virtual-area names or build identifiers fail rather than truncate. Flag and version ioctls have distinct widths between native long and 32-bit integer compat forms, so careless reuse corrupts high bits. Policy query and scan structures rely on caller-supplied size for versioning, so stale sizes misinterpret trailing fields. Key removal must handle busy files and other users as separate output conditions rather than simple success, and incomplete removal persists as a distinct presence state.
